subject: mathematics
question_text: If A + B + C = π/2, then prove that cos 2A + cos 2B + cos 2C = 1 + 4 sin A sin B sin C.

mark_split.label: Replace A + B by π/2 − C
Replace sin C inside the bracket

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.107 — from the book's separate "STAR QUESTIONS PLUS" bank, answer 168. That bank (book pp.98-111, answers 142-180) sits AFTER all the numbered chapters and is organised by chapter rather than forming part of any chapter's own inventory; it is authored into this unit because that is where the question belongs on the paper (founder decision 2026-08-22). SECTION: classed LAQ on its length and shape — a transformation identity on a triangle, the exact shape of Unit 6's own LAQ chapter. The bank prints no mark cut, so this classification is OURS. Printed appearances: AP 20 · TS 19. The condition here is π/2, NOT π. Every substitution has to use the right one — reaching for A + B + C = 180° out of habit breaks the proof. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — the bank prints no [N Marks] tags anywhere. The shapes used follow the splits the book DOES print elsewhere: 1+1 for a 2-mark VSAQ (answers 100, 101 on book p.82), 1+1+1+1 or 1+2+1 for a 4-mark SAQ (answers 58, 59 on p.63 and 61 on p.64), and the granular split for a 7-mark LAQ (answer 32 on p.44). This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

steps.label: Group the first two terms
steps.margin_note: Two of the seven marks. cos C + cos D = 2 cos((C+D)/2) cos((C−D)/2), applied to cos 2A + cos 2B.

recall.must_convey: That cos 2A + cos 2B becomes 2 cos(A+B) cos(A−B).
accept: group the first two and apply cos C plus cos D to get two cos of A plus B into cos of A minus B
the halves cancel leaving A plus B and A minus B
apply the sum to product formula to the first two terms
modati rendu group chesi sum to product apply cheyyali
convert the first pair to a product

steps.why: The 2s inside cancel against the halves in the formula, so the messy 2A and 2B become plain A + B and A − B.
common_mistakes: Grouping cos 2B + cos 2C, which does not lead anywhere useful.
Forgetting to halve the sum and difference.

steps.label: Replace A + B by π/2 − C
steps.margin_note: Third mark. From A + B + C = π/2, A + B = π/2 − C, and cos(π/2 − C) = sin C.
lines: ⇒ cos(A + B) = cos(π/2 − C) = sin C
L.H.S = 2 sin C cos(A − B) + cos 2C

recall.must_convey: That A + B = π/2 − C gives cos(A + B) = sin C.
accept: A plus B is pi by two minus C so its cosine is sin C
cos of pi by two minus C is sin C
use the given condition to turn the cosine into a sine
A plus B ante pi by two minus C, cos adi sin C
apply the angle condition

steps.why: A cosine becomes a SINE under this shift — which is exactly what the right-hand side needs, since it is a product of three sines.

steps.label: Expand cos 2C
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. cos 2θ = 1 − 2 sin²θ. This choice, out of the three forms of cos 2θ, is what produces the 1 on the right-hand side.
lines: L.H.S = 2 sin C cos(A − B) + 1 − 2 sin²C

recall.must_convey: That cos 2C = 1 − 2 sin²C, and 2 sin C is factored out of the remaining two terms.
accept: cos two C is one minus two sin squared C and then take two sin C common
use the form of cos two theta that gives a one
the one comes straight from the double angle formula
cos two C ni one minus two sin square C ga rasi two sin C common teeyali
expand the double angle and factor

steps.why: cos 2θ has three forms. Only 1 − 2 sin²θ leaves a standalone 1, which is the first term on the right-hand side.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to keep the 1 outside the bracket.

steps.label: Replace sin C inside the bracket
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Inside the bracket, write sin C as cos(A+B) — the reverse of step 2 — so both terms become cosines.
lines: Inside the bracket, sin C = cos(π/2 − C) = cos(A + B)

recall.must_convey: That sin C inside the bracket is written as cos(A + B), giving cos(A−B) − cos(A+B).
accept: write sin C inside the bracket as cos of A plus B so both terms are cosines
reverse the substitution inside the bracket only
the bracket becomes cos A minus B minus cos A plus B
bracket lo sin C ni cos A plus B ga marchali
substitute back inside the bracket

steps.why: The sin C outside stays and the sin C inside converts — the bracket needs two cosines before the difference formula can be used.

steps.label: Apply the difference formula
steps.margin_note: Last mark. cos(X−Y) − cos(X+Y) = 2 sin X sin Y with X = A, Y = B gives 2 sin A sin B.
lines: cos(A − B) − cos(A + B) = 2 sin A sin B
L.H.S = 1 + 2 sin C · 2 sin A sin B

lines.text: ∴ cos 2A + cos 2B + cos 2C = 1 + 4 sin A sin B sin C

recall.must_convey: That cos(A−B) − cos(A+B) = 2 sin A sin B, giving 1 + 4 sin A sin B sin C.
accept: cos A minus B minus cos A plus B is two sin A sin B so the answer is one plus four sin A sin B sin C
the two twos multiply to four
the bracket becomes two sin A sin B and closes the proof
bracket two sin A sin B, rendu twos kalisi four
apply the difference formula and close

steps.why: The 4 on the right comes from two separate 2s — one from step 3's factoring and one from this formula. Neither is arbitrary.
common_mistakes: Writing the bracket as 2 cos A cos B.
